facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells admixed with rare eosinophils
hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts
identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes
A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells admixed with rare eosinophils
hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts
identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes

concepts.why: The patient's new-onset eruptive facial lesion, characterized by a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells admixed with rare eosinophils, uniformly positive for CD207/langerin, is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

The patient's chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome, refractory anemia with excess blasts, and hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts are consistent with myelodysplastic syndrome with excess blasts.
The patient's myelodysplastic syndrome with excess blasts and hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts may progress to acute myeloid leukemia.
The patient's new-onset eruptive facial lesion, characterized by a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells, may be consistent with leukemia cutis.
The patient's identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1 gene, identified through next-generation sequencing, are consistent with an ASXL1 mutation.
The patient's identical pathogenic variations in the IDH2 gene, identified through next-generation sequencing, are consistent with an IDH2 mutation.
The patient's identical pathogenic variations in the STAG2 gene, identified through next-generation sequencing, are consistent with a STAG2 mutation.
The patient's BRAF-V600E variant status, identified through immunohistochemical studies and confirmed by polymerase chain reaction analysis, is consistent with a BRAF-V600E mutation.

concepts.why: The skin biopsy finding of atypical dermal infiltrate cells negative for myeloperoxidase explains the uncovered fact.

rationales.F07: The absence of myeloperoxidase staining is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, particularly the subtype with myeloperoxidase-negative cells.

rationales.F10: The presence of identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes is suggestive of a shared genetic abnormality.
